sections.title: Tree and blossom
sections.text: The common pear is a deciduous European and western Asian tree, often 8–12 m tall with a 4–8 m spread in cultivation. It bears clusters of white spring flowers; wild trees may be thorny.

sections.title: Fruit and food
sections.text: Its pear-shaped to nearly round fruits can reach about 10 cm and are eaten fresh or cooked. Cultivated size depends strongly on variety and rootstock. The consulted sources did not identify a specific toxicity concern for the edible fruit.

sections.title: Image details
sections.text: The plate shows the white blossom, a toothed leaf, and whole and cut pears with their seeds, matching the species.
